study.title: Automatic assessment of collaterals physiology in chronic total occlusions by means of artificial intelligence

imaging.modality_detail: Coronary X-ray angiography (cine) pre and post CTO-PCI, monoplane systems
imaging.territory_detail: Coronary arteries: CTO artery and primary/secondary collateral donor arteries

annotation.annotator_expertise: Experienced interventional cardiologists grading Rentrop and CC collaterals; third interventional cardiologist as referee for disagreements

task.task_description: Automatic computation of donor-artery flow velocity pre and post CTO-PCI from the length/time curve of contrast filling derived from deep-learning (U-Net) coronary segmentation, used to derive collateral flow change and collateral flow index, compared against Rentrop and CC angiographic grading.
task.clinical_application: Physiologic assessment of coronary collateral circulation in chronic total occlusion PCI without dedicated wires or devices

temporal_evidence.quote: Taking into account the frame rate, the curve of vessel length variation over time (length/time curve) could easily be derived during the phase of contrast injection.

method.pretraining: U-Net segmentation model previously validated in a prior study (ref 13); applied without retraining description

metrics.metric: Feasibility of automatic AI analysis (105 of 112 patients)

G2.quote: the accuracy of the method at 7.5 frames/s is essentially unknown and should be specifically addressed in future studies

G6.quote: This was a retrospective study, thereby with the intrinsic limitations of this design, and potentially subject to selection bias.

G11.quote: an eventual prognostic value of the collateral closure, which could be evaluated in sequential follow-up studies

other_limitations: No head-to-head comparison with intracoronary Doppler or pressure wire
No comparison with invasive absolute coronary blood flow by thermodilution
Delta-CFI only approximates CFI because collateral flow persists after PCI
future_work: Head-to-head validation against intracoronary Doppler or pressure wire
Comparison with thermodilution-derived absolute coronary blood flow
Evaluate method in retrograde CTO approach
Evaluate prognostic value of collateral closure in follow-up studies
